subject: Encryption & KMS options — FinServe follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@finserve.com>, security@finserve.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Encryption & KMS options — follow-up from today's call

Hi Oliver / FinServe security team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps on encryption and key management items you asked about: 

- In-transit: We use TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 recommended) for all client-server and inter-service connections. Mutual TLS can be enabled for private deployments.
- At-rest: Data stored by Redwood is encrypted using AES-256. For Hosted (SaaS) customers we use provider-managed keys by default.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): Supported for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. Options include:
  - Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS) where we either reference customer keys or use a customer-managed HSM depending on the deployment.
  - HSM-backed keys via KMIP or managed HSMs for Dedicated setups where physical/key isolation is required.
- Key rotation & rotation policies: We support rotation and can align rotation windows and notification hooks with your security ops requirements.
- Logging and plaintext exposure: We do not log request/response plaintext by default. Sensitive fields can be redacted, and we can provide tailored logging configs for Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: We can pin data to specific regions / VPCs on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API we offer regional endpoints; please confirm which region(s) you require (you mentioned us-east-1).

I've attached a short KMS options overview and our SOC 2 summary. Next suggested steps:
- Quick follow-up (30 min) with Dev Patel to go over Azure Key Vault specifics and any integration constraints.
- Share any required contractual language (DPA / encryption clauses) so we can review.

Proposed times for a technical call: Tue 12/15 2:00–4:00pm PT or Thu 12/17 9:00–11:00am PT. Please let me know what works.

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (PDF), soc2-summary.pdf (PDF), network-diagram.png (PNG)

Thanks,

—

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) We run everything in Azure; can you integrate with Azure Key Vault (AKV) for CMKs, and do you support Managed HSM?
2) What does key rotation look like — can we retain control over rotation schedules and retain historical key versions for audits?
3) Do any of your logs or telemetry ever contain unredacted PII or plaintext payloads? If so, can that be disabled for our account?
4) Data residency: we need guaranteed storage in us-east-1 only. Is that possible for Dedicated/Private? What about Hosted?
5) Can you share a network architecture diagram and the SOC 2 summary (for compliance review)?

If you can answer these and include any sample contract language around CMK/rotation/log access it would speed our procurement/security review. Looking to schedule the technical call — Thu 12/17 9:00am PT works for our security engineer.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — follow-up from today's call

Hi Oliver — short answers below and attaching the requested artifacts. See attached: redwood-kms-options.pdf (details by deployment), soc2-summary.pdf, network-diagram.png.

1) Azure Key Vault / Managed HSM: Yes — we support AKV integration for Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated we can integrate with your AKV via a network peering and reference keys (or use Managed HSM for stricter isolation). For Private (on-prem or VPC) we can support bring-your-key/imported keys or an HSM appliance.

2) Rotation: We support configurable rotation windows. Customers retain control over rotation cadence for CMKs. We also retain historical key versions per KMS provider semantics for auditability; we can provide rotation logs as part of the compliance package.

3) Logs & PII: Our default logging excludes request/response bodies and any unredacted PII. For Dedicated/Private we can further harden logs and disable certain telemetry streams. We can provide a log-handling/retention matrix in the DPA.

4) Region residency: Dedicated and Private allow strict region/VPC residency (us-east-1 available). Hosted can be restricted to a regional endpoint but if you need physical separation and contractual data residency guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private.

Next steps:
- Confirm Thu 12/17 9:00am PT for a 30-min technical call with Dev Patel and your security engineer.
- If you want specific contract language, flag the clauses and we will loop legal.

Available times: Thu 12/17 9:00am PT confirmed by your note. I'll send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (PDF) — includes AKV, AWS KMS, GCP KMS flows and HSM options; soc2-summary.pdf (PDF); network-diagram.png (PNG)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-17T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Encryption & KMS options — internal notes

Marissa / Mike — quick internal tech notes ahead of the call with FinServe: 

- AKV integration: Supported for Dedicated via private peering. We can either reference keys (no key material leaves FinServe) or perform key wrapping depending on their preference. Managed HSM is supported where they require FIPS/HSM-backed keys.
- Hosted constraints: Hosted SaaS uses provider-managed keys by default; CMK support is available only for enterprise commitments with dedicated infrastructure.
- Rotation & audit: Rotation handled by the underlying KMS; we persist key version metadata and rotation events to our audit logs (no plaintext). We should confirm exact retention window FinServe needs and include an audit export option.
- Logs & PII: Confirmed — no plaintext payloads stored. For extra assurance we can provide a gating transform that redacts known PII fields before hitting the model for Dedicated/Private.
- Contract language: Suggest we offer a DPA clause that states: "Customer retains control of CMKs; Redwood will not export key material; Redwood will provide rotation logs and audit exports on request." Legal should review but it's a good start.

I'll join the Thu 12/17 9:00am PT call. Will prepare a one-page KMS integration diagram and the recommended DPA snippet to share.

—
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
